title: The Best 433 MHz Wireless Temperature Sensors
subtitle: Indoor-outdoor thermometers and replacement sensors on the 433 MHz band.
intro: We pulled the 433 MHz wireless temperature sensors selling on Amazon and scored them on rating, review volume, and features. These are standalone sensors and displays; the guide below explains how hobbyists read them in Home Assistant.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

scoring.review_age_weighting: Listings under 24 months old with at least 30 reviews have their review count multiplied by min(2, 24 / age in months, age floored at 6) before scoring; older listings are unchanged. Listing age is Amazon's Date First Available, or an estimate from the ASIN when the listing does not show it.

buyers_guide.q: Can a 433 MHz sensor work with a smart home?
buyers_guide.a: Not on its own. These sensors talk to their own display. With a cheap USB SDR receiver and the rtl_433 software, Home Assistant can read many AcuRite, La Crosse, and Ambient Weather sensors, but that's a do-it-yourself project, not a supported feature.

buyers_guide.q: Will a replacement sensor work with my display?
buyers_guide.a: Only if the listing names your display's model. 433 MHz sensors use brand-specific formats, so an AcuRite sensor won't pair with a La Crosse display.

buyers_guide.q: Where should an outdoor sensor go?
buyers_guide.a: In the shade, out of direct sun and rain, and a few feet off the ground. A sensor in the sun can read 10°F or more too high.
